content.title: Is Now a Good Time to Refinance? How to Know If the Math Actually Works (2026 Update)
content.text: Is now a good time to refinance your mortgage in 2026 — or is waiting actually the smarter move? With mortgage rates down from their 2022–2023 peak but still well above pandemic lows, many homeowners are asking whether refinancing makes sense right now. In this video, Erin Moriarty from Erin Talks Money breaks down the real math behind refinancing, using updated 2026 mortgage rate data, break-even analysis, and practical alternatives most homeowners overlook. This isn’t hype or rate-watching. It’s a calm, data-driven guide to understanding when refinancing actually saves money — and when it doesn’t. You’ll learn: Current 30-year and 15-year mortgage rates in early 2026 Why Federal Reserve rate cuts don’t directly control mortgage rates How to calculate your refinance break-even point using real numbers When refinancing makes sense — and when it absolutely does not Why the common 0.75% refinance rule is incomplete How closing costs, loan terms, and time horizon affect total savings Smarter alternatives to refinancing, including mortgage recasts, principal paydowns, and PMI removal What to do if your mortgage rate is high but refinancing doesn’t pencil out yet How to position yourself now so you’re ready when rates change This video also explains: Mortgage rates vs. the federal funds rate Why mortgage rates are driven by long-term bond markets, not short-term Fed decisions 2026 economic projections, inflation trends, and what they realistically mean for homeowners How aggressive early principal payments can dramatically reduce interest over time Why many homeowners refinance too early — and how to avoid that mistake Whether you bought a home during the 2022–2023 rate spike, are considering refinancing in 2026, or simply want to understand how mortgage math really works, this video will help you make a confident, informed decision — without guessing or chasing headlines.
